Question B-007-006-007.

Why the correct answer is right: The 20-metre band sits in a reliable part of HF for daylight long-distance work. Solar maximum often improves higher bands, but 20 metres is usually capable of worldwide daylight openings somewhere in every part of the cycle.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Only at the minimum point of the solar cycle": Solar minimum does not uniquely enable 20 metres; if anything, lower solar activity makes higher paths less generous.
- sourceIndex 2: "Only at the maximum point of the solar cycle": Solar maximum helps, but 20 metres is not limited to peak years.
- sourceIndex 3: "At the beginning of the solar cycle": The beginning of a solar cycle is near the low, rising part of the cycle; it is not a special boundary that alone determines 20-metre daylight propagation.
